author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Massachusetts drivers were paying an average of about $4.24 a gallon for regular gasoline Wednesday, according to AAA figures cited by Boston 25 News, as another rise in crude oil intensified concern about household and business costs.

The station reported that oil gained more than 3% during Wednesday’s session. The national gasoline average was about $4.22, compared with roughly $3.19 a year earlier. The Massachusetts figure was described as a record for this point in the calendar. These numbers reflect the source’s Wednesday snapshot and should not be read as live prices.

The impact extends beyond fuel pumps. Diesel prices feed into trucking and delivery costs, while heating oil remains an important winter expense for many New England households. Sustained increases can reach grocery shelves and service bills as companies pass along higher transportation and operating costs.

Day-to-day prices can move quickly with crude markets, refinery conditions, regional inventories and distribution constraints. The latest increase therefore does not establish where costs will settle for the heating season. It does, however, sharpen the region’s affordability concerns just as residents and fuel suppliers begin preparing for colder weather.
dek: AAA figures cited Wednesday put regular gasoline near a seasonal record, while higher crude prices renewed concern about diesel, heating oil and transportation costs.
headline: Massachusetts gas average reaches about $4.24 as oil rally raises winter concerns
